rules.title: Notice to quit for nonpayment of rent under a written lease
rules.requirement: For nonpayment of rent under a written lease, a landlord may end the lease with 14 days' written notice to quit. The tenant can keep the tenancy by paying all rent due, with interest and costs, on or before the answer day in an eviction action. If the nonpayment was caused by a government delay in mailing or delivering a rent or subsistence payment, the court must continue the hearing at least 7 days and treat the tenancy as not terminated if all rent is paid in that time.
rules.quoted_span: Upon the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due under a written lease, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the lease
rules.key_value: 14 days' written notice to quit for nonpayment
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to tenancies under a written lease where rent is unpaid.

parsed.doc_summary: Massachusetts G.L. c. 186, § 11: 14 days' written notice to quit for nonpayment of rent under a written lease, with a tenant right to cure and a court continuance when the nonpayment was caused by government payment delays.
